correctness.rationale: The idempotent equation in the specified natural basis is x=Aᵀx^[2]. Its fixed space is binary-linear. In a minimal nontrivial dependence among binary-independent fixed vectors over F_q, normalize one coefficient and compare the relation with its semilinear image. The remaining vectors are F_q-independent, so every coefficient equals its square, contradicting binary independence. Thus the fixed dimension is at most s by containment in im(Aᵀ). For an F_q frame of r fixed-point candidates, its squared frame spans an r-plane. The kernel must miss this plane. The kernel is uniform and the transverse kernels are graph lifts of (n−s)-planes in the quotient, giving q^{r(n−s)}[n−r:n−s]_q choices. Conditional on transversality, the image frame is uniform by left GL_n invariance. Summing over all candidate frames cancels its cardinality and gives the claimed moment α. Division by |GL_r(2)| converts frames to binary subspaces; binary Gaussian inversion gives the signed formula. The r=0 moment is one; rank zero has only zero as idempotent, and rank one gives the stated Bernoulli law. Equivalently α=∏_{j=0}^{r−1}(1−q^{j−s})/(1−q^{j−n}), so it is identically one for s=n and tends to one at fixed n,s. The latter moments are exactly those of uniform GL_s(2) by transitivity on binary r-frames, completing the limit.
residual_risks: Six small field/dimension enumerations were reported, not freshly run. Exhaustion there is not evidence of exhaustion elsewhere. The proof needs uniform labelled matrices and characteristic two.

evidence: The survey has a random evolution algebra question and the mean on invertible matrices; Fulman–Goldstein concerns the rank statistic itself.
The later full-matrix result gives the law aggregated over all ranks and an aggregate conditioned only on singularity; its large-n limit fixes q.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The marginal rank law alone does not determine a statistic within exact rank strata. A single mixture over singular ranks does not invert to the individual conditional laws. The fixed-q large-n limit is not the fixed-n,s large-q limit here.

evidence: Known perfect-matrix formulas have ordered-frame moments equal to one. The new conditional moment has the nontrivial q-dependent kernel-transversality factor α; for rank one it gives q^{n−1}(q−1)/(q^n−1).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: An invertible fixed-space law, the first moment at full rank, and an aggregate singular law do not imply those q-dependent exact-rank moments. The new count treats how a prescribed candidate frame meets the random kernel before applying the fixed-frame method. The limiting GL_s(2) law is a consequence of these moments, not a new GL_s(2) distribution formula.

Invertible semilinear descent does not equate each singular rank-s map to an invertible s-dimensional map with that same law: already the finite-q rank-one probability is less than one for s<n.

originality.rationale: The exact law on each singular rank stratum, and its fixed-rank field-size limit, are the distinct contributions. The perfect-algebra distribution and the binary fixed-frame and Gaussian inversion methods are established ingredients. Exact full-rank and all-matrix laws must not be credited to this record.
residual_risks: Bounded literature and index comparison cannot exclude an equivalent unindexed distribution for uniformly rank-conditioned Frobenius-semilinear matrices. Algebra isomorphism classes and random labelled matrices remain separate ensembles.

value.rationale: Rank is a natural invariant of the algebra's multiplication image. Conditioning on it identifies what the perfect law and the mixture hide: finite-field variation already at rank one, exact probabilities up to the maximal possible idempotent count at any rank, and a universal binary fixed-space limit at fixed rank. The complete conditional classification is more informative than the unconditional mean or a finite table.
residual_risks: No conclusion about random isomorphism classes, other matrix ensembles, odd characteristic, or growth of n with q.
